t: None of the funds appropriated or otherwise made available in this Act may be used to transfer any individual detained at United States Naval Station Guantanamo Bay, Cuba, to the custody or control of the individual’s country of origin, any other foreign country, or any other foreign entity except in accordance with section 1034 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2016 (Public Law 114–92) and section 1034 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2017 (Public Law 114–328).

fable.w: This is an appropriations limitation that bars using funds to transfer Guantanamo detainees except in accordance with two cited NDAA sections. The tempting reading is that the mention of foreign countries or entities, or the cross-referenced NDAA sections, implies coordination with outside parties. That fails because the foreign countries are only recipients of detainees, and the text itself creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with non-federal parties, or right to sue.
fable.s: None of the funds appropriated or otherwise made available in this Act may be used to transfer any individual detained at United States Naval Station Guantanamo Bay, Cuba

qwen_block.w: This section is a funding restriction that prohibits the use of appropriated funds for specific transfers of detainees. It does not establish any mechanism for consultation, coordination, or participation by outside parties (such as the public, states, or NGOs) in the decision-making process. The reference to other sections of law defines the conditions under which transfers might occur, but this specific text imposes a prohibition rather than inviting external input.
qwen_block.s: None of the funds appropriated or otherwise made available in this Act may be used to transfer any individual detained at United States Naval Station Guantanamo Bay, Cuba, to the custody or control of the individual’s country of origin, any other foreign country, or any other foreign entity except in accordance with section 1034 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2016 (Public Law 114–92) and section 1034 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2017 (Public Law 114–328).

opus.w: This section only limits how appropriated funds may be spent on detainee transfers, by pointing to section 1034 of two defense authorization acts. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. The foreign country or entity is just where a detainee would be sent, not a party consulted before the decision. Any process in the cross-referenced sections (as I recall, certifications to Congress) would stay inside the federal government.
opus.s: None of the funds appropriated or otherwise made available in this Act may be used to transfer any individual detained at United States Naval Station Guantanamo Bay, Cuba, to the custody or control of the individual’s country of origin, any other foreign country, or any other foreign entity except in accordance with section 1034
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The section mentions handing detainees over to a foreign country or "foreign entity," which could look like coordination with a party outside the federal government. That reading fails. Handing someone over to a foreign government is the federal action itself. It is not outsiders being consulted before a federal decision. The only process is a cross-reference to section 1034 of two defense authorization acts. As I recall from background knowledge, those sections involve certifications and notices to Congress, which is inside the federal government. They aren't in the text here in any case.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a funding restriction that prohibits the transfer of detainees unless specific statutory conditions are met. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties (such as the public, states, or foreign entities) within this text. The reference to other sections of law does not constitute participation in this section itself.
qwen_chat.s: None of the funds appropriated or otherwise made available in this Act may be used to transfer any individual detained at United States Naval Station Guantanamo Bay, Cuba, to the custody or control of the individual’s country of origin, any other foreign country, or any other foreign entity except in accordance with section 1034 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2016 (Public Law 114–92) and section 1034 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2017 (Public Law 114–328).
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the reference to "section 1034" implies a process involving outside parties (like state governors or foreign governments) that constitutes participation. However, the text itself does not describe that process; it merely restricts funding based on compliance with other statutes. The section itself contains no mechanism for outside consultation, comment, or coordination.
